To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PlGF is a novel cytokine involved in Wallerian Degeneration, a peripheral nervous system degeneration process.

PlGF is expressed in the peripheral nervous tissue, that its expression is regulated by NF‐κB, and that its absence results in a delayed macrophage invasion in a model of Wallerian degenerative injury, with consequences on nerve functional recovery.

PlGF is expressed in Schwann cells, that its expression is upregulated in the first 24 h after injury, that PlGF is required for macrophage recruitment and that PlGF deficiency leads to worse functional recovery after sciatic nerve injury.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of Wallerian degenerative process in the peripheral nervous tissue, and the role played in this process by placental growth factor.
the role of PlGF in Wallerian Degeneration.

the molecular and cellular mechanisms that underlie the development, maintenance, and regeneration of the peripheral nervous system (PNS) with the aim to identify potential targets for the treatment of peripheral nerve diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have shown that PlGF plays a significant role in Wallerian nerve degeneration.
Pgf−/‐ mice show an impaired WD process, with a delayed macrophage invasion and a reduced expression of MCP‐1 and ProMMP‐9, which results in a delayed functional recovery.
Pgf is an important player in WD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PlGF is a key player in the inflammatory response of WD, and that PlGF deficiency delays macrophage invasion in the injured sciatic nerve.
PlGF is an essential factor of the cytokine/chemokine network involved in Wallerian Degeneration, and that it acts as a positive regulator of the inflammatory process.
Pgf−/‐ mice exhibit a delayed macrophage invasion in Wallerian Degeneration (WD) compared to wild‐type mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PlGF is a novel member of WD cytokine network.
PlGF is a key player in WD.
PlGF is involved in the process of Wallerian degenera‐tion.
